symptom: Dropping a Studio Pro microflow and creating it from its own DESCRIBE output changed the diagram: loop boxes recomputed (and grew into neighbours, MPR008), every merge shrank from 90x60 to 40x40, a type split with a returning case lost its merge position (rebuilt on top of the first branch), and a merge closing both an if and the if nested in its branch became two merges stacked at the same point.
cause: MDL had no spelling for a box size (@merge took x, y only; loops and while-true head merges had no @size); commonMergeAfter required EVERY branch to reach the merge, but the type/enum split builders close the split with a merge as soon as any case continues; and one merge per block meant a shared merge was built once per block.
fix: @merge(x, y, w, h) and @size(w, h) (loop box, while-true head merge, merge <label>), printed only when not the default; type/enum splits search the merge over the cases that continue (two at least); collapseCoincidentMerges folds a merge whose only exit goes to a merge at the same position and size.
insight: Measure on a whole app, not one flow: a harness that snapshots every merge and loop box (position;size) before, drops + creates the 41 flows that have one, and diffs after went 30 diffs -> 0 for these classes, and each fix moved a different flow off the list. What remains is the single-path merge DESCRIBE already warns about (#923, no MDL spelling) - a flow whose only merge is one of those vanishes from a geometry snapshot entirely, which reads like a failed create. Live on 11.16.1: mx check 0 errors, second exec 40 unchanged.
test: mdl/executor/issue2369_geometry_test.go (each builder site with a revert proof; continuing-branch merge search with commonMergeAfter as control; distinct nested merges kept)
